owner_brief: the owner, 2026-10-05, during the play test: 'need to make a way for players to earn money playing through minecraft game loop, like selling minerals in brocks town or something.'

mechanism.summary: CobbleDollars' own Bank. Every CobbleDollars merchant (cobbledollars:cobble_merchant: every stall keeper in data/markets.json, Hollin's apricorn stall, the BCA shopkeepers of data/traders.json) opens it on shift + right-click, or from the Bank button on its shop screen. The player puts items in and presses Sell; each stack is paid at the bank's unit price times its count. The price list is ONE server-wide file, config/cobbledollars/bank.json: no per-merchant, per-town or per-player list exists in the installed version. So the buyer in Brock's town is every merchant on Stoneford's square, and the same buyer stands in every town that has a merchant; tiering is by WHAT is sold (deep ores and rarer drops pay more), not by where.
mechanism.rung: configuration (CLAUDE.md principle 6): a mod's documented config file, no datapack, no function, no NPC. The cheaper rung (Cobblemon native) has no sell-back; the next one (an addon already installed: CobbleDollars) has it, and its list is a config file
mechanism.why_not_a_dialogue_buyer: a dialogue NPC that takes N items with `clear` and pays with `cobbledollars give` would be the functions rung. It would buy per town at per-town prices, but it adds a purchase function per item, a menu per town and a double-submit guard, to do what the bank already does for every item at every merchant. Nothing in the owner's ask needs a per-town price; nothing here is a written failure of the bank. Kept as the fallback if the experiment below fails
verified: CobbleDollars-fabric-2.0.0+Beta-5.1+1.21.1.jar (the server's installed copy, the jar file only), read 2026-10-05 with python zipfile and javap:

fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.network.handlers.server.SellHandler.handle: requires the player's open menu to be a BankMenu, takes SimpleContainerExtensionsKt.getBankableItems(menu.getBankContainer()), and for each stack adds CobbleDollars.INSTANCE.getBankConfig().getBank().get(stack).getPrice() x count to PlayerExtensionKt.getCobbleDollars(player), then setCobbleDollars. No merchant, town or player key is read: the list is global

the same handler never reads CommonConfig: cobbleDollarsIncomeMultiplier is read only in fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.event.CobbleDollarsEventsKt (battle victories, NPC and wild). So the bank is NOT scaled by our 1.25 multiplier (answers docs/mechanics/PROGRESSION_LADDER.md U-1 statically; not run in game)

fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.world.item.trading.shop.Bank extends ArrayList<Offer> with get(ItemStack); the match is MiscUtilsKt.isSame, which compares the item AND its data components (method_57353), so a renamed or otherwise changed stack does not sell

fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.config.BankConfig: PATH = "config/cobbledollars/bank.json"; the only field is `bank` (BankAdapter reads the key `bank`, an array of the shape base-pack/cobbleverse/config/cobbledollars/bank.json carries: {item, price})

fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.world.entity.CobbleMerchant.mobInteract (method_5992): player.isShiftKeyDown (method_5715) -> PlayerExtensionKt.openBank, else openShop. The entity's only own NBT key is CobbleMerchantShop: there is no per-merchant bank field

fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.client.gui.screen.ShopScreen builds a BankButton that sends OpenBankPacket(merchant UUID); OpenBankHandler opens the bank for any entity that is a CobbleDollarsShopHolder

fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.command.CobbleDollarsCommand: literals cobbledollars (alias cd), give, remove, set, query, pay, leaderboard, reload. `reload` calls BankConfig.Companion.load, CommonConfig.Companion.load and ShopConfig.Companion.load and sends SyncShopConfigPacket(defaultShop, bank) to players: a new bank.json takes effect without a restart
mechanism.what_else_pays: trainer battle victories, by CobbleDollarsEventsKt (earnCobbleDollarsFromNPC true, scaled by cobbleDollarsIncomeMultiplier 1.25, in modpack/config/cobbledollars/common.json). afk_rule.independence: this list is the builder's; tools/economy_audit.py AFK_FARMABLE is the auditor's own, separately derived (2.3). The two are never merged

farm.why: vanilla 1.21.1 items a farm makes once built, the chunk loaded and nobody acting: crop farms (villager farmers, observers), tree farms, melon, pumpkin and sugar cane observer farms, kelp into furnaces, AFK fishing, berry and cave-vine harvesters, nether wart and budding-amethyst harvesters. Mob farms are not here: every vanilla mob they need is on the mobsbegone blacklist (server/config/mods/mobsbegone-blacklist.json), and the mobs' drops that Pokemon also make are in `ranch`

ranch.why: Pasture Loot (pastureLoot-1.0.5, installed): a pastured Pokemon has a 15% chance a minute to drop from its own species drop table, minus modpack/config/PastureLoot.json item_blacklist (our overlay of the base pack's file; tools/bank.py PASTURE_LOOT) (docs/research/OBTAINABILITY_VANILLA_COBBLEMON.md, relayed; the drop mechanics ASSUMED to work as configured). So every species drop the blacklist does not name is an unattended farm once a player owns the species
ranch.measured: 2026-10-10, from the offline snapshot C:/Users/wnd/Documents/cobblers-local/server-snapshot-2026-10-05 (mods/*.jar and datapacks/*.zip, every data/<ns>/species and species_additions JSON's drops.entries[].item), against the bank as it stood before this change (base + buys, 122 entries): these are the bought items a species drops and the blacklist does not name. `python tools/bank.py check --server-dir <snapshot>` re-measures it. rules: the output is the base file's entries in their order, unchanged, followed by `buys` in their order: CobbleDollars reads one file, so ours must carry the base's list too (tools/markets.py bank_prices reads base then ours and agrees with this)
a `buys` item already in the base is refused: changing a base price is a separate, named decision

base_removed: a base entry leaves the output only through base_removed.entries, each with its base price for the record, its afk source and its why; the decision is named once (the owner, 2026-10-10). An entry naming an item the base does not carry is stale and refused

afk_rule (fails closed): nothing in afk_rule.farm, afk_rule.ranch or afk_rule.crafts is bought, and no `buys` entry is in an afk_rule.groups group, unless afk_rule.exceptions names it with a why and a decision. An exception for an item that is not bought, or not in the rule's lists, is stale. With --server-dir the ranch list is re-measured from the species drop tables in the server's jars and datapacks, and a bought drop the list does not name is refused
buys_removed: every entry this file once bought and no longer does keeps its old record and its reason; it may not also be in `buys`
every price is a positive whole number (the file's own shape; Offer.price is a BigInteger)

no item is bought that any authored shop sells at or below the bank's price: buy-low-sell-high is free money (tools/markets.py's own rule, applied here to every sell point the tool can read; see tools/bank.py for the list and what it does not cover)

never_buy holds: the evolution stones (the faces restore every 600 s and the Exchange never buys, data/traders.json stock_policy.stones), every block a spawn condition names (data/spawn_blocks.json: paying for one pays players to strip encounters out of the world), and the storage blocks that craft back into a bought item
a bought item whose id is a spawn-condition block is allowed only when `in_place` is true: the item comes from harvesting a block that stays where it is (in_place_evidence)
a smelted item pays at least its raw ore and at most raw + 2: smelting is worth a little, never a lot (a furnace and fuel are the cost)
every town in buyer_towns has at least one sited CobbleDollars merchant (a data/markets.json stall), so the bank opens there
a crafted item in `crafts` pays its inputs' bank total to that total + CRAFT_MAX, and every input is bought or named by crafts.removed_inputs (valued at its buys_removed price)
a smelted item and its raw ore are bought together, except an ingot afk_rule names and buys_removed records (the raw ore still sells)
no `unreachable` item is in `buys` (one the BASE buys is reported as dormant, not failed: changing a base price is a separate decision)
effort_model: every tier holds parity and upper_wage (R5) against data/markets.json income_basis.leg_by_badge

every data/markets.json stock line with exchange_for: its material is bought here, its price is exactly count x the material's price, it sits on a sited OFF-PATH counter in a town exchanges.where names (never a stall, never the critical path), its `kind` is one of exchanges.kinds and it clears that kind's floor, and the bank never buys the reward back
in_place_evidence: an apricorn's and a berry's item id is also its block's, and data/spawn_blocks.json names those blocks (Pineco, Morpeko and others need them near). Selling the fruit does not take the block out of the world: Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.0+1.21.1.jar, ApricornBlock.harvest drops the fruit (method_9497) and sets AGE to 0 on the same block (method_8652), so the fruit regrows where it hung; BerryBlock.harvestBerry pops BerryBlockEntity.harvest's berries and sets no block (read with javap 2026-10-05). Breaking the block by hand still removes it; that is true with or without a price

effort_model.label: ESTIMATE. Every rate is ASSUMED (no one has timed an hour of gathering in this world); the leg incomes are RELAYED from data/markets.json income_basis.leg_by_badge (model B), not measured. The model fixes the SHAPE of the prices; EXP rates replace the numbers
effort_model.owner_brief: the owner, 2026-10-06: 'I want ordinary Minecraft play to be worth doing ... real Minecraft effort converted into Pokemon progression ... priced so it is an alternative path, not a shortcut past the economy.'
effort_model.derivation: a tier's gathering hour is the sum over its items of rate_per_hour x price (rate_per_hour_upper where an item names one, for the upper hour). A unit price is the tier's target hour shared over what one hour of that tool in that place yields, rounded to a whole dollar; a smelted item pays raw to raw + 2 and a crafted one its inputs to inputs + CRAFT_MAX, so no step is worth skipping or worth doing for its own sake
effort_model.max_leg_hours_why: ASSUMED: a badge leg is played in at most four hours. If EXP timing finds legs longer than this, battling pays less per hour than assumed and the gathering hours below come closer to it: re-price then
effort_model.rules_decision: docs/mechanics/ECONOMY_OVERHAUL.md section 7 R5 (2026-10-10): 'half_wage becomes parity ... upper_wage becomes the upper hour <= 1.5 x the fight hour'. The owner now wants Minecraft to pay early, so parity, not half. The fight hour is the leg's battle income / max_leg_hours
rules: parity: a tier's typical hour is at most the fight hour of the leg where the tier opens (that leg's battle income / max_leg_hours). Gathering at the typical rate pays at most what fighting pays: an equal path, never the better plan
upper_wage: a tier's upper hour (bed, TNT, Fortune: the efficient method) is at most upper_factor (1.5) x that fight hour. The best grinder earns at most half again what a fighter earns

half_wage: a tier's typical hour x max_leg_hours is at most half the battle income of the leg where the tier opens. Gathering at the typical rate pays at most half of fighting: worth doing, never the better plan

upper_wage: a tier's upper hour (bed, TNT, Fortune: the efficient method) x max_leg_hours is at most the whole battle income of that leg. The best grinder earns at most what a fighter earns: an alternative path, not a shortcut

exchanges.barter_answer: a CobbleMerchantShop cannot take items as payment. CobbleDollars-fabric-2.0.0+Beta-5.1+1.21.1.jar (the snapshot's copy), read 2026-10-06 with javap: fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.world.item.trading.shop.Offer holds only `item` (ItemStack), `price` (BigInteger) and `stock` (int); Shop$Companion reads an offer's NBT keys Item, Price and Stock only (Stock absent = -1, unlimited; a set Stock is per merchant and shared by every player); network.handlers.server.BuyHandler.buy compares PlayerExtensionKt.getCobbleDollars with the price, subtracts it with setCobbleDollars and gives the stack (method_7270). No item cost is read anywhere. So the exchange is two halves of one merchant: shift + right-click sells the material to the Bank (this file's `buys`), the shop screen sells the reward at the CobbleDollar value of the effort (data/markets.json stock lines carrying `exchange_for`)
exchanges.shape: every exchange line is a counter stock line in data/markets.json with exchange_for {item, count}: its price is EXACTLY count x what this bank pays for that item, so 'a Master Ball for thirty netherite ingots' is literally true at the same merchant: sell thirty ingots at the Bank, buy the ball from the shop. The dollars are the same dollars a battle pays, so a fighter can buy the same line: the exchange is an alternative path to the reward, priced so neither path is the shortcut (effort_model)
exchanges.where: the off-path counters whose shelves the ladder gates on a badge (PROGRESSION_LADDER 1.2): Fossick's Mine Stores (mining_town, gym3_cleared), the deep-ore exchange priced in diamonds; Northlight's Station Supply (northlight, gym6_cleared), the Nether exchange priced in netherite ingots. NOT the critical-path counters (Holdfast, Cinderlee): every line there is on the price curve, and a $27,000 line would carry badge 8's cumulative ask out of the 0.65-0.70 band. NOT the ungated off-path counters (Redbrow, Steepside, Pacifidlog): a ball, held or evolution item there is an ungated power line, which tools/town_squares_audit.py lists as a known defect

floors.why: each kind's floor is read from what the shelves already sell, never a tuned constant: an exchange must not make power cheaper than the ladder already prices it

held_item.why: the held items the counters sell today (the type boosters, data/markets.json); the floor is the dearest of their unit prices

ball.from: every line on every counter and stall that is not an exchange line: a Master Ball is dearer than anything else for sale

kinds.evolution_item: an item a species needs to evolve and the world has no reachable recipe or source for (the Cobblemon 1.8.0 jar's recipes, read 2026-10-06). Floor: never cheaper than an evolution stone (data/traders.json stock_policy.stones.price, the region's one stone price)
kinds.held_item: a battle held item with no reachable recipe (its recipe names a blaze powder, scute, everstone or steel gem). Floor: dearer than every held item a counter already sells
kinds.ball: the Master Ball: Cobblemon 1.8.0's own recipe is a netherite ingot + a nether star + a shulker shell (data/cobblemon/recipe/master_ball.json), and the star and shell are unreachable here, so the game itself already says netherite -> Master Ball. Floor: dearer than every other line on any shelf. A Master Ball does not pass the level cap (data/level_cap.json: a Pokemon over the thrower's cap breaks free from every ball)

income_estimate.early_hour: stone pickaxe, caves above y0, the first two hours: coal 60 x $4 + raw iron 30 x $8 + raw copper 40 x $2 + lapis 15 x $4 = $620 an hour
income_estimate.deep_hour: iron pickaxe, deep caves: the early hour plus raw gold 10 x $20 + redstone 25 x $2 + diamond 4 x $120 = $1,350 an hour

income_estimate.against_the_ladder: battle income to badge 1 is $9,475 (data/markets.json income_basis, model B, relayed). If leg 1 takes about three hours (ASSUMED), battles pay about $3,150 an hour, so mining pays a fifth to two fifths of fighting. A player who mines for one hour on the way to Brock adds $620-1,350: the Mart basics ($1,600 a leg, PROGRESSION_LADDER 0.3) or one counter line, not the shelf. Stoneford's critical ask is $6,000 of the counter plus $7,500 for the crafting upgrade; buying that upgrade by mining alone is 6-12 hours, by picking apricorns 5-7
income_estimate.what_it_does_not_buy: the curve (tools/markets.py curve) is NOT changed: it still prices against battle income alone. Gathering is the margin a player who digs earns, not a term the shelves were priced on
